# PREFIX-851 — Exact modular recovery after a burst of missing named BRC heartbeats

**Research scope:** abstract positive-integer, Q-only, *named* BRC scalar observer; not a native X6 event law.
**Date:** 2026-11-17. **Status:** AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FINITE_REGRESSION / NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED.
**Frozen science input:** f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d (unchanged).
**Dependency:** PREFIX-847–850, especially PREFIX-850's synchronized one-update observer.
**Control:** independent auxiliary research; no shared RS-X6-NATIVE-TIME-DYNAMICS CLAIM is asserted.

## 1. Question, typed BRC carrier, and information boundary

There are p named initial positive BRC sources. Each source weight is 1 or 2; its 0/1 increment is x_i=w_i−1. The names i=0,...,p−1 are retained (no permutation quotient). Pack their increments into
U(x)=sum_{i=0}^{p−1}2^i x_i, 0≤U<2^p.

At each *auxiliary discrete update* at most one named source is changed, including no change. These update indices are not automatically physical heartbeat durations. The declared positive-integer Q observer returns at time t≥1:
Y_t(x)=c_t(S_0+U(x)) mod m, c_t=2^{floor(t/2)}, where S_0 is known.

The decoder possesses the **complete named state x_s** at one prior synchronization time s. It then loses observations for r≥1 updates and obtains one Y_{s+r}; it knows r and the coefficient. A state reachable at that point differs from x_s at Hamming distance at most r, and every state in that Hamming ball is reachable (flip its differing bits, then use no-change steps). This is a burst-erasure/resynchronization extension of PREFIX-850, not the autonomous decoder of PREFIX-848/849.

The observer is only claimed sufficient for the named binary weights and specified transitions after the known baseline. Hidden branch histories, native Cell/Link/Port provenance and later operations that need them are **not** quotiented away by this auxiliary scalar.

## 2. Exact fixed-modulus correction criterion

Write H_r(z)={x in {0,1}^p : dist_H(x,z)≤r}. For positive odd q>1 define

D_{p,r}={ |sum_{i in I} eps_i 2^i| : 1≤|I|≤min(2r,p), eps_i∈{−1,+1} }.

All members are nonzero because the largest power of two exceeds the sum of smaller distinct powers.

**Theorem 851-A (necessary and sufficient).** A fixed *odd* raw modulus q supports exact recovery from any old named state after any r consecutive lost observations, at every later observation time, if and only if

  for every d in D_{p,r}, q does not divide d.

**Proof.** Since q is odd, c_t is invertible modulo q. Subtracting S_0 after multiplying by its inverse gives U(x) modulo q. For any two states x,y, their difference U(x)−U(y) is a signed sum of 2^i over exactly the bit positions in x XOR y. Two states lie in a common r-Hamming ball exactly when dist_H(x,y)≤2r: the forward inequality is the triangle inequality; conversely divide their differing bit positions into two sets each of size at most r and construct an intermediate z agreeing with x on one and y on the other. Thus a uniform ambiguity exists precisely when q divides one of the displayed nonzero signed sums. QED.

**Corollary 851-B (fixed raw moduli).** For any integer raw modulus m≥2 used at all future times, put q=m/2^{v_2(m)}. Uniform all-future correction is possible exactly when q>1 satisfies Theorem 851-A. Any fixed modulus with a power-of-two factor eventually exposes no more information than its odd part, because c_t is a growing power of two. Consequently the optimal all-future raw modulus is odd:

  q*(p,r)=min{odd q≥3 : q divides no d in D_{p,r}}.

The optimal single-read port width in this declared modular-observer family is ceil(log_2(q*(p,r))). The decoder stores the p-bit previous state; the port-width figure does not include this side information.

## 3. Universal bounds and exact near-saturation transitions

**Theorem 851-C.** For every p,r≥1, with N=2^p and V(p,r)=sum_{j=0}^{min(p,r)} C(p,j),

  V(p,r) ≤ q*(p,r) ≤ N+1.

If 2r<p, the stronger upper bound q*(p,r)≤N−1 holds.

If 2r≥p, then **q*(p,r)=N+1**.
If 2r=p−1, then **q*(p,r)=N−1**.

**Proof.** Every r-ball contains V(p,r) states, so injectivity into q residue classes requires q≥V. A modulus q=N+1 distinguishes every integer U in [0,N−1], proving the first upper bound. When 2r<p, q=N−1 has only one possible distinct colliding pair in [0,N−1], namely (0,N−1), whose Hamming distance p exceeds 2r; hence it works. If 2r≥p, every two states lie in some common ball and full injectivity requires q≥N, whose smallest admissible odd value is N+1. If 2r=p−1, any odd q<N−1 collides on the pair (0,q), because the p-bit expansion of q has at most p−1=2r nonzero digits. The previous N−1 upper bound is attained. QED.

**Relation to PREFIX-850.** For r=1, signed differences have support at most 2. Theorem 851-A reduces exactly to the projective binary order condition h(q)≥p. Thus PREFIX-850 is the one-missed-update case of this stronger erasure theorem.

## 4. Finite exact minima and examples

A self-contained Python integer checker enumerates every signed sparse difference, all its odd divisors, and excludes all smaller odd moduli. It additionally crosschecks the predicted classification by *directly constructing all predecessor Hamming balls* for every odd q≤q*(p,r) for p≤6 and at q* and q*−2 for 7≤p≤8.

The exhaustive range is p=1,...,13 and 1≤r≤min(3,p): **36 exact finite optima**. No random or floating-point comparisons are used. Reproduction:
python research_notes/portable_direct/PREFIX851_R6_BURST_ERASURE_BRC_CHECK.py
This generates the adjacent JSON result with exclusion witnesses and per-case digests.

| p | r=1: q* | r=2: q* | r=3: q* |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|1|3|—|—|
|2|5|5|—|
|3|7|9|9|
|4|11|17|17|
|5|11|31|33|
|6|13|59|65|
|7|19|107|127|
|8|19|171|251|
|9|19|171|491|
|10|23|205|939|
|11|23|359|1707|
|12|29|557|2731|
|13|29|565|2731|

Example: p=5, after one missed update q*=11 (4 bits); after two q*=31 (5 bits); after three q*=33 (6 bits). At two erasures, 0 and 11 have Hamming distance 3 and lie together in the radius-2 ball of an appropriate predecessor. Hence modulus 11, although optimal when just one update is missed, cannot resynchronize after two. Modulus 31 is optimal by Theorem 851-C's 2r=p−1 equality.

A non-extremal instance is p=6,r=2 with q*=59 (six bits). All 28 smaller odd moduli from 3 through 57 have a concrete signed-difference divisibility witness; the checker exhaustively verifies them. The lower information bound is V(6,2)=22, so the actual BRC readout shape imposes additional constraints beyond mere state counting.

## 5. Proof and execution limits, control, and next frontier

The general statements are elementary exact combinatorial/algebraic theorems of the **declared** positive-integer named BRC Q observer. The finite checker establishes only the enumerated ranges and is not independent mathematical peer review. None of these statements licenses a native X6 Cell/Link/Port observation, equates auxiliary updates to physical heartbeat ticks, discards the source/carry/branch history needed for future operations, or changes P000.

One genuinely unresolved question: for fixed r≥2 and arbitrary large p, determine the growth of q*(p,r) under binary positional powers, with a quantitative construction or lower bound beyond the Hamming-ball cardinality. Also study rejoining with an uncertain (rather than fully known) prior state, missing/inaccurate r, and typed native event realizability; these are different interfaces.

Publication is an author-level research checkpoint only, with unchanged source firewall, no formal Result/Review, and no assertion of active shared ownership.
